extracted.intended_audience: aspiring memoirists and creative writers (students, authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for crafting a personal memoir, with emphasis on voice, truthfulness, sensory detail, memory, and ethical handling of subjects. Focused on helping writers choose details, shape emotional stakes, and preserve authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive voice emerges from lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiences and emotions, their distinctive voice emerges and becomes clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should grow out of the author's experiences and emotional truth rather than imitation; self-awareness helps the voice to be authentic and relatable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-awareness and confronting psychological conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-awareness is crucial for a memoirist because it helps them confront and express their psychological conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-examined life enables the author to craft a voice that is authentic and relatable; writers should interrogate their motives, failures, and inner life to produce honest narrative perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confess darker traits and experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Confessing darker traits and experiences adds depth and honesty to a memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are drawn to genuine vulnerability and recognition of flaws; confession enhances relatability and authenticity. Avoid sanitizing or omitting morally difficult material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance humor and pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: A memoirist can balance humor and pathos by allowing their personality to shine through while also being candid about their struggles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixing light and dark creates nuance; don't let humor undercut seriousness nor let pathos make the voice monotonous—use tone shifts to reflect complexities of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional stakes drive engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional stakes are significant because they create drama and engage readers on a personal level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share intense experiences and feelings so readers feel the weight of moments; stakes give urgency and compel reader investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice tied to truth and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A powerful voice in memoir writing is intimately tied to the truth of the author's experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The voice conveys authenticity so readers can trust the storyteller; maintain integrity and be vigilant against fabrication or sensationalism that undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deceit and fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoirists should strive for accuracy while acknowledging that memory can be flawed; beware of embellishment or fabrication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr warns against liars in memoir and the cultural appetite for sensationalism; maintain honesty even when memory is imperfect—fabrication damages the genre and reader trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnality — evoke the five senses
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnality—the ability to evoke physical sensations through the five senses—is essential in memoir writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific sensory details to make scenes vivid and believable; sensory recall creates immersive moments that connect readers physically and emotionally to the memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use totemic, specific details
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose specific items or memories as focal points (totemic details) that anchor scenes and emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Maya Angelou's Easter dress, Chekhov’s watermelon—pick details that are original, evocative, and emotionally resonant rather than generic descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, don't tell (sensory immersion vs generic statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than telling readers what happened, writers should show experiences through the lens of physical sensations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid broad statements or abstract emotional reportage (anti-pattern: 'telling' writing, ascribed to Robert Graves); prefer precise, sensory-laden description (as in Michael Herr) to pull readers into lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory as material — emotional truth over literal accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory shapes the details and the emotional truth of the narrative; memories may not always be perfectly accurate but their sensory and emotional cores can convey deeper truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept memory's slipperiness; use sensory and psychological truth to make scenes believable while being cautious about factual claims that could be verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice observation to strengthen sensory memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers can improve sensory-rich writing by practicing observation and attentiveness to the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in exercises focusing on all five senses, reflect on personal experiences, and regularly revisit memories with sensory emphasis to build vividness in scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the most original, evocative detail
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting among memories, favor the recollection that feels most original and evocative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogate multiple recollections and pick the detail that best captures the emotional core and feels fresh—avoid clichés or vague memories that lack specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use objects/metaphor to carry emotional meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Object description can serve greater narrative purposes by transforming everyday objects into vessels of memory and philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage metaphors and recurrent objects (e.g., cradle/coffin, household artifacts) to structure themes and to preserve beauty or meaning against loss (Nabokov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend realism and myth/fantasy when useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Blending personal narrative with cultural mythology or fantasy can deepen storytelling and reflect complex identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maxine Hong Kingston’s use of myth enriches memory and cultural history; use such blending intentionally to illuminate emotional or cultural truths rather than to hide factual ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interiority — foreground inner life and internal conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Interiority represents the internal struggles and emotional landscapes that distinguish great memoirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal psychic struggles, failures, fears, and inner enemies to create resonance; interiority drives theme and character development more than external events alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the 'inner enemy'—explore failures and fears
rubrics_metrics.description: A memoirist confronts their inner enemy by exploring failures, fears, and conflicts which shaped identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate psychic struggle and consequences; such confession creates compelling narrative and invites reader empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace emotional intensity; avoid emotional distancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers should embrace authentic emotional intensity rather than distance themselves from feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional intensity fuels compelling memoirs; avoid cool detachment that can leave narratives flat (Atwood example of anxiety in process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed facts within lived scenes (don't let data dominate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts are necessary but should be woven into scenes that evoke emotion rather than presented as dominant, flat information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with fact-heavy drafts if needed, then transform facts into scenes that dramatize and humanize the information; avoid information-dumps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present age/physical traits through action and image
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey physical or demographic facts indirectly through evocative scenes or actions rather than blunt statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: show size through an action (brushing a basketball net) or self-consciousness (struggling into a jacket) to give psychological depth to the fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on a single character or moment to humanize larger facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than broad exposition, center scenes on a person or moment to make broader themes relatable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orwell’s technique of connecting to a single freedom fighter is cited—this approach humanizes political or social facts by anchoring them in personal detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dramatic imagery to captivate
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic imagery captivates readers by inviting them into the scene rather than simply telling facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft vivid, evocative descriptions (e.g., gripping hands) that create emotional impact and make readers care about events and characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision process: transform information-dense drafts into scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with initial drafts full of facts and then work to convert that information into lived, remembered scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision should focus on connecting facts to personal experience and sensory detail, reshaping data into narrative that feels lived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical handling of real people in memoirs
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for dealing with family and friends: notify subjects in advance, avoid showing mid-process, emphasize love, and maintain humility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr’s rules: inform those portrayed, allow them to express concerns, keep dialogue open, and balance honesty with respect. These practices aim to minimize harm while preserving truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether to collaborate or write independently
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoirists vary: some interview and collaborate with family, others write independently with little concern for reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider gendered tendencies and the implications of collaboration; choose an approach consistent with the writer’s ethics and the work’s aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sharing unfinished pages mid-process
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not show mid-process pages because it can interfere with the writer's vision and dilute the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share polished work instead; early reactions can derail developmental choices and compromise the integrity of the final piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid posturing and inauthentic language
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs of posturing include forced references or language that doesn't align with the author's identity (trying to seem 'cool').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest about voice; feedback from others can help detect posturing. Authentic diction tied to personal background tends to resonate more genuinely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charm — ability to make the mundane engaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Charm refers to the writer's ability to engage and hold the reader’s attention, making mundane events feel interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A charming voice uses personality and specificity to transform ordinary moments; use wit, voice, and detail to captivate without sacrificing truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contrast/twinning to reveal resonances
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Twinning' is a device to contrast moments from the past, revealing deeper thematic parallels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairing scenes or images can emphasize interconnectedness and produce thematic depth that transcends single events (as Nabokov does).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge memory's limits while asserting responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory is slippery and partial, but writers have a responsibility to pursue truth and clarity in their narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisit the past to gain perspective and integrate past traumas carefully; be transparent where memory is uncertain and avoid presenting speculation as verified fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cultural narratives to reclaim identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers can use family stories and cultural myths to reclaim or reinterpret identity (e.g., Kingston’s reclaiming of female identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave collective or familial stories to chart personal transformation; respect the cultural context and be mindful of representational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from stylistic contrasts between authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare different authors to understand effects: e.g., Herr’s visceral specificity vs Graves’s telling abstractions; Nabokov’s ornate diction vs typical memoir narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze other memoirists to determine which techniques produce emotional authenticity and reader connection; adopt methods that serve your material.
